info.name: Vuelto API
info.description:
Complete API surface of the Vuelto app (rename per app — see docs/REBRANDING.md).

**Setup**
1. Import `vuelto.local.postman_environment.json` and select it.
2. Start the stack: `docker compose up -d` (Postgres + Mailpit) and the API (`dotnet run --project src/Api --launch-profile https`).
3. SMTP must point at **Mailpit** (`localhost:1025`) for the OTP auto-fetch to work — if your `.env` overrides SMTP to a real provider, switch it back for API testing.

**Sign-in flow (folder 1):** `OTP — send` → `OTP — fetch code from Mailpit` (delivery is async; wait ~2–5 s after send) → `OTP — verify`. Tokens are stored in the environment and every request in the collection authenticates with them automatically. Auth requests send `X-Native-Client: true`, selecting the body token transport (no cookies needed in Postman); the refresh token rotates on every `Refresh` call.

**MFA:** if the account has MFA enabled, `OTP — verify` stores a `mfaChallenge` instead of tokens — run `MFA — verify (step-up)` with a TOTP or recovery code.

**Admin folder** needs the signed-in user's email in `Admin__StaffEmails__0` (API restart required). **Public API / Webhooks folders** are config-gated default-off (`PublicApi__Enabled=true`, `Webhooks__Enabled=true`).

request.description: Rate-limited 5/min per IP (429 after — QA-AUTH-11). Email delivery is async (outbox): wait a few seconds before fetching the code.

item.name: OTP — fetch code from Mailpit (local envs only)

request.description: Reads the newest Mailpit message and extracts the 6-digit OTP into {{otpCode}}. Only works in environments with a mailpitUrl (local). On hosted envs (staging/prod) email goes to REAL inboxes — read the code there and set {{otpCode}} manually (or paste it straight into 'OTP — verify').

exec: console.warn('This environment has no Mailpit (hosted env — real email). Read the OTP from your inbox and set {{otpCode}} manually.');
if (!msgs.length) { console.warn('Mailpit is empty — send the OTP first; delivery is async (wait ~2-5s).'); }
else console.warn('No 6-digit code in the newest email — is it the OTP email?');

header.description: Body token transport — refresh_token returned in JSON instead of a cookie (Postman-friendly).

request.description: Stores accessToken/refreshToken on success. If the account has MFA enabled, stores mfaChallenge instead — run 'MFA — verify (step-up)' next. 401 invalid_code = wrong/expired; 401 too_many_attempts = cumulative lockout (QA-AUTH-04); 429 = throttle.

exec: console.log('MFA required — challenge stored. Run: MFA — verify (step-up).');

request.description: Completes sign-in for an MFA-enabled account. Accepts a 6-digit TOTP or a single-use recovery code (case/hyphen/space-insensitive). Challenge is single-use and short-lived (~5 min).

exec: if (json.access_token) { pm.environment.set('accessToken', json.access_token); if (json.refresh_token) pm.environment.set('refreshToken', json.refresh_token); console.log('Step-up complete — tokens stored.'); }

request.description: Rotates the refresh token (old one is revoked; replaying it revokes every session — reuse detection). The stored refreshToken is updated automatically.
The verify half is a browser redirect flow (GET /api/auth/magic-link/verify?token=&email= → 302 to the web app) — click the link from Mailpit in a browser; it isn't meaningful as a pure API call.

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). Full-page navigation: 302 to the provider's consent screen. {provider} = a configured provider from GET /api/auth/providers. No auth; errors land on the client's /auth-error.

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). The PROVIDER redirects here after consent (carries its code/state). Issues the session (refresh cookie) and 302s to the client. Never called by an API client directly.

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). The emailed magic-link URL. Single-use, hashed, time-limited token in the query; consumes it, sets the refresh cookie (or MFA step-up redirect), then 302s to the client.

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). Opened in the OS browser by MAUI clients (WebAuthenticator). Like /login/{provider} but the callback returns a deep link carrying a one-time code instead of a cookie.

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). Provider redirect for the native flow: issues a short-lived ONE-TIME CODE and 302s to the app's custom-scheme deep link. The code is redeemed via POST /api/auth/native/exchange.

Redeems the one-time code from the native callback deep link for tokens on the BODY transport (access + refresh token JSON; no cookie). 400/401 invalid_code on unknown/expired/replayed codes (single-use, 5-min TTL); {mfa_required, challenge} when the user has MFA enabled — step up via POST /api/auth/mfa/verify. Requires the X-Native-Client: true header.

en / es shipped. Drives UI + email language. Follows the user across devices: applied (with one reload on mismatch) on every sign-in, and a device-local login-page choice is adopted here automatically on sign-in when unset (PREFS-1, ADR-022). With an impersonation token as bearer → 403 impersonation_not_allowed (server-side guard, v3 ADM-8).

light / dark / system (THEME-1 + PREFS-1, ADR-022). All three are stored verbatim and follow the user across devices — "system" means follow the OS scheme; null in the DB means "never chose" (lets sign-in adopt a device-local choice). Lands in the JWT on the next refresh. Anything else → 400 unsupported_theme. With an impersonation token as bearer → 403 impersonation_not_allowed (server-side guard, v3 ADM-8).
Fail-closed: refuses to remove your last sign-in method (QA-SET-05). Link-start (POST /api/auth/link/{provider}) is a browser redirect flow.
GDPR erasure — IRREVERSIBLE. Owner-with-members → 400 (transfer first). Sole owner → 409 until confirm_dissolve=true (which also dissolves the household).

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). Starts linking an additional OAuth provider to the signed-in account: responds with the provider redirect carrying a short-lived link token; completes at the callback with ?linked=… (or ?link_error=…) on the client's /settings. Requires the Bearer token.

**Documentation-only — a browser flow, not runnable from Postman.** Listed so the collection stays a complete mirror of the API surface (v3 audit TR-6; the parity gate `PostmanParityTests` enforces it). Time-limited signed download URL minted by the export/file surfaces (FILES-2; the token IS the authorization — DataProtection-signed, tenant-scoped). Browser navigation; responds with Content-Disposition: attachment.
Returns the otpauth:// provisioning URI + Base32 secret (shown once). Add the secret to an authenticator app, then Confirm.

exec: if (json.secret) { pm.environment.set('mfaSecret', json.secret); console.log('Secret (add to authenticator):', json.secret); console.log(json.provisioning_uri); }

request.description: Enables MFA and returns the 10 one-time recovery codes (xxxxx-xxxxx) — logged to console, shown ONCE.

exec: if (codes) console.log('RECOVERY CODES (save now, shown once):', codes.join(', '));

request.description: Returns the raw token ONCE (also emailed). 402 = seat quota reached (QA-HH-14). 409 = already a member.

Sign in as the invitee first (re-run folder 1 with the invitee email) — accept joins the CALLER to the inviting household. Errors: 400 invitation_invalid/must_transfer_first/would_abandon_data, 409 already_member, 402 seat_limit_reached when the household downgraded below its reserved seats (BILLING-9 — the token stays pending and works again after an upgrade).
Roles: member | admin (owner is transferred, never assigned). Owner-only.
Owner-only; you become a member afterwards.
Member: leaves + re-homes to a fresh solo household. Owner with members: refused (transfer first). Sole owner: needs confirm_dissolve=true (dissolves).
GDPR export. Returns a signed, time-limited download URL (stored as {{exportDownloadUrl}} — use 'Files — download export'). Metered per plan (402 when the monthly quota is spent).

exec: if (url) { pm.environment.set('exportDownloadUrl', url.startsWith('http') ? url : pm.environment.get('baseUrl') + url); console.log('exportDownloadUrl stored'); }

request.description: The signed URL from the export (GET /api/files/{token}); no bearer needed — the token IS the auth, and it expires.

Clears ALL of the caller's notifications. The scope is REQUIRED (v3 LB-UI-10): read=false = all, read=true = only read; omitting ?read is a 400 (scope_required), so delete-all can never be hit by a dropped param.
Plan, status, seats — owner-only (403 otherwise).
Returns the provider checkout URL (fake provider locally: billing.test/... — won't load, by design).

header.description: The FAKE provider accepts the literal 'valid' (dev only). Real Stripe uses stripe CLI / real signatures.

request.description: Upgrades {{tenantId}} to pro/active as if checkout completed (QA-BILL upgrade loop). Requires the FAKE provider (dev default) — on an environment wired to real Stripe (test mode), this returns 400 invalid signature by design; use `stripe trigger` there instead. Run 'Get household' first to populate {{tenantId}}. Re-sending the same EventId is deduped (inbox); an older OccurredAt than the last applied event is ignored.

item.name: 8 · Admin (platform staff)
item.description: Requires the signed-in user's email in Admin__StaffEmails__0 (repo .env) + API restart. Non-staff → 403 everywhere except 'Am I staff'. An impersonation token ({{impersonationToken}} as bearer) → 403 impersonation_not_allowed on every staff action, and 'Am I staff' reports false — staff powers never transit a sign-in-as session (v3 ADM-2).

exec: if (list.length) { pm.environment.set('adminTenantId', list[0].id); console.log('adminTenantId =', list[0].id, '(' + list[0].name + ')'); }

item.name: Announce to tenant (all members or user_ids subset)

request.description: user_ids: null/omitted = every member; a NON-empty list = just those (intersected with the roster); an explicitly-empty [] = NO ONE (v3 LB-ADM-2). Audited in-tenant.
Queued (202) — the outbox dispatcher fans out a few seconds later. ADR-021.

Simulates a completed checkout (active, never lapses, no provider ids). 409 = tenant has a LIVE Stripe subscription — keyed on liveness (status ≠ canceled), so a churned/canceled tenant is comp-able even though it kept its Stripe id (ADR-006/021, v3 ADM-5).
Deletes the projection (absence ⇒ Free). Idempotent. 409 = LIVE provider subscription (status ≠ canceled); a canceled-but-lingering projection is cleaned up, not blocked (v3 ADM-5).

Stores {{impersonationToken}} (does NOT overwrite your session). To act as the target, temporarily set a request's bearer to {{impersonationToken}}. ~15 min, non-refreshable, audited in the target's tenant.

exec: if (pm.response.code === 200) { pm.environment.set('impersonationToken', pm.response.json().access_token); console.log('impersonationToken stored (expires_in:', pm.response.json().expires_in + 's)'); }

request.description: Staff recovery path (ADR-021 addendum): wipes the user's TOTP secret + recovery codes WITHOUT a code — verify their identity out-of-band first. Also REVOKES the target's refresh tokens/sessions (v3 ADM-7 — compromise recovery). Audited in the target's tenant (admin.mfa.reset) and the user is notified (in-app + email). 204 also when the user had no MFA (idempotent no-op).

item.name: 9 · Public API & keys (config-gated)
item.description: Default OFF — set PublicApi__Enabled=true (repo .env) + restart. Key management is owner-only JWT; /api/public/* authenticates with the key itself.

request.description: Raw pk_ key returned ONCE — stored as {{apiKey}}.

exec: if (json.key) { pm.environment.set('apiKey', json.key); console.log('apiKey stored (shown once):', json.prefix + '…'); }

request.description: Key → tenant-scoped principal. Also accepts Authorization: Bearer pk_… . Per-key rate limit: 60/min → 429.

item.name: 10 · Outbound webhooks (config-gated)
item.description: Default OFF — set Webhooks__Enabled=true (repo .env) + restart. Owner-only. Target URLs must be public-routable (SSRF guard blocks localhost/private ranges) — use https://webhook.site or similar.

request.description: Signing secret (whsec_…) returned ONCE — stored as {{webhookSecret}}. 400 = SSRF guard rejected the URL.

exec: if (json.secret) { pm.environment.set('webhookSecret', json.secret); console.log('webhookSecret stored (shown once)'); }

request.description: Synchronously POSTs a signed test 'ping' and returns { delivered, status_code } (or { delivered:false, error:'delivery_failed' } on a transport error). Records a WebhookDelivery row for the attempt (success and failure), so the Delivery log is populated immediately — run it, then the Delivery log request.

Recent delivery attempts for this subscription (newest first, tenant-scoped): each row has success, status_code, error, event_id. Populated by Send test event (sync) and by published/replayed events (async via the outbox). Captures the newest row's id into {{deliveryId}} for Replay.

Re-enqueues the exact stored payload of {{deliveryId}} (same event id, so a receiver can dedup) → 202; delivered async via the outbox with retry/backoff, which logs its own attempt row. 404 for an unknown or other-tenant delivery id.
